Wallie, saw Sonatus is pushing deeper into agentic AI for software-defined vehicles alongside partners like Nissan and Schaeffler.

Landing OEM and tier-one deals at that pace usually means more in-market accounts than business development can cover before interest fades. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Sonatus off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Wallie, quick follow-up for Sonatus.

In long automotive sales cycles, most teams can't say how many qualified meetings they need to feed the pipeline that converts a year out, so the gap surfaces late and recovering it gets expensive.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Sonatus needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Wallie, last bit of proof for Sonatus.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Sonatus's reply rate likely compares to other venture-backed tech companies. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?

Wallie, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling business development without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Standing up agentic AI motions with new OEM partners is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise automotive motion? I'll tailor it to Sonatus either way.
